blocks.summary: Rescind sanctions on the International Criminal Court
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: The recommendation was to lift or rescind the sanctions on the International Criminal Court; instead the United States maintained them and in 2025 imposed further sanctions (Executive Order 14203), including against the Court's judges and staff.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 25 — Several special procedure mandate holders: "condemned the executive order imposing sanctions on the International Criminal Court ... by sanctioning the Court, the United States weakened the post-Nuremberg commitment to international criminal justice"

blocks.summary: Prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity

blocks.summary: Protect access to asylum and non-refoulement; limit immigration detention
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Access to asylum was severely curtailed, detention without due process expanded and family separation resumed - directly contrary measures.

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 90 — JS47: "at the US-Mexico border, asylum had been all but eliminated"

blocks.summary: Honour Indigenous treaties and guarantee free, prior and informed consent
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Executive Order 14112 on Tribal self-determination and funding was revoked in March 2025; FPIC is still not guaranteed in law or practice.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 58 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination; Human Rights Committee: "recommended that the United States honour the treaties entered into with Indigenous Peoples, guarantee, in law and in practice, the principle of free, prior and informed consent"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 83 — Several submissions (OHCHR summary): "Executive Order 14112, which had expanded access of Tribal Nations to federal funding and self-determination ... was revoked in March 2025"

recommendations.text: Implement deliberate strategies to reduce the gap between African-Americans and the rest of the population, as well as between indigenous and non-indigenous populations, and hence reduce structural and institutional discrimination

blocks.summary: Eliminate violence against women and girls

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 70 — GFG (Global Freedom Group): "reported funding cuts to the Violence Against Women Act and domestic violence programmes"

Address further the issue of sexual violence in the military

blocks.summary: Eliminate violence against women and girls

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 70 — GFG (Global Freedom Group): "reported funding cuts to the Violence Against Women Act and domestic violence programmes"

recommendations.text: Prioritize services for preventing and responding to gender-based violence, including in institutional settings such as the penitentiary system
Vigorously continue measures directed at the elimination of violence against women and girls

blocks.summary: Climate-change mitigation and adaptation
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Contrary measures: renewed withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and 2025 executive orders reviving fossil fuels and abolishing decarbonisation targets.

recommendations.text: Advance towards the implementation of instruments to combat climate change and its negative impacts on human rights
Intensify efforts to develop and strengthen the necessary legislative frameworks that address cross-sectoral environmental challenges, including climate change adaptation and mitigation frameworks
Pursue the fight against the global problem of climate change and its negative impacts, in particular by strengthening cooperation with the international community in this area

blocks.summary: Clean up toxic contamination affecting minority communities
blocks.rationale: Toxic-waste clean-up in disproportionately affected communities was still being urged; no national plan. 'Noted'.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 49 — Special Rapporteur on racism: "recommended urgently cleaning up toxic waste and environmental contamination, particularly in areas where it was having a disproportionate impact on marginalized racial and ethnic groups, including in the overseas territories"

recommendations.text: Respond appropriately to the substance of the relevant recommendations made by the Special Rapporteur on the implications for human rights of the environmentally sound management and disposal of hazardous substances and wastes in the 2012 report on his visit to the United States and the Marshall Islands

blocks.summary: End excessive use of force

recommendations.text: Continue efforts to limit armed violence and crimes by regulating the possession and use of arms

Take further and more targeted measures to address the disproportionate impact of violence on the poor, minorities and immigrant women, and expedite the ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women and the Convention on the Rights of the Child

themes.theme: Prohibition of torture & ill-treatment (including cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment)

blocks.summary: Criminalise torture and provide redress for rendition victims
blocks.rationale: No specific federal offence of torture was enacted; rendition-programme victims remain uncompensated.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 21 — Human Rights Committee: "the United States should review its position regarding the establishment of a specific offence of torture, enact legislation prohibiting torture in line with international law"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 27 — Special Rapporteur on ... human rights ... while countering terrorism: "none of the former detainees had been compensated for the systematic crimes of extraordinary rendition, torture, cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment and arbitrary detention"

recommendations.text: Prohibit torture in detention and ensure detainees have access to fair trials and full redress

blocks.summary: End arbitrary detention
blocks.rationale: No indication of change; recommendation 'noted'.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 26 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination: "highlighted the continued arbitrary detention of non-citizens at the Guantanamo Bay facility, without effective and equal access to the ordinary criminal justice system"

recommendations.text: End the arbitrary detention of many Iranians under bogus allegations of violating its unlawful sanctions

blocks.summary: Close Guantanamo and end indefinite detention
blocks.rationale: Twenty-five detainees were transferred from Guantanamo Bay since the last review and some conditions improved, but 15 men remain in indefinite detention and the facility is not closed.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 28 — Amnesty International: "15 men were still arbitrarily and indefinitely detained at Guantanamo Bay, following the transfer of 25 detainees since the previous review"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 28 — Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms while countering terrorism: "urged the United States to close the Guantanamo Bay detention facility, while preserving it to ensure independent and effective investigation of torture"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 28 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended expediting the transfer of detainees designated for transfer from that facility and putting an end to administrative detention without charge or trial"

Close Guantanamo and guarantee the rights of detainees
Close as soon as possible the Guantanamo detention centre
Close totally illegal extraterritorial prisons, especially at Guantanamo, a territory illegally occupied by the United States

blocks.summary: Federal moratorium on / abolition of the death penalty

evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 20 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended establishing a de jure moratorium on the death penalty at the federal level and taking steps towards its abolition"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 15 — The Dui Hua Foundation: "Executive Order 14164 reinstating capital punishment for federal crimes, for which a moratorium had been imposed in 2021"

Defer or suspend the application of the death penalty and expedite the adoption of a federal law to comply with the ruling of the International Court of Justice in the Avena case

Consider abolishing the death penalty

blocks.summary: Prevent gun violence

Take measures to combat systemic racism and police violence against people of African descent

recommendations.text: Take effective measures to prevent trafficking in persons and to address the issues of overcrowding in prisons, police violence and the increase in manifestations of racism, extremism and xenophobia

blocks.summary: Combat trafficking in persons
blocks.rationale: The Human Rights Committee still recommends redoubling efforts and stakeholders report continuing failures in victim identification.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 38 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended that the United States redouble its efforts to combat trafficking in persons by improving victim identification, strengthening its preventive measures"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 49 — JS22: "reported failures in identifying and supporting victims and securing criminal convictions"

recommendations.text: Continue to improve efforts to reduce and eliminate adult and child trafficking
Strengthen its bilateral collaboration to abolish human trafficking and slavery in the fisheries industries
Continue efforts in combating human trafficking and ensure the protection of the rights of victims of trafficking, as well as the rights of migrants

themes.theme: Labour rights and right to work

blocks.summary: Working conditions, minimum wage and forced prison labour
blocks.rationale: Forced prison labour continues and the right to work is reported to have worsened, with mass terminations of federal employees in 2025.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 30 — Special Rapporteur on racism: "referred to reports of poorly paid or unpaid forced labour by prisoners, who were disproportionately from racially marginalized groups"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 50 — Elizka Relief Foundation: "observed a worsening of the right to work, including reduction and terminations of federal employees and precarious employment of migrants"

recommendations.text: Strengthen sanctions against employers who engage in unfair labour practices and ensure that workers ’ rights are not violated

blocks.summary: Address poverty, inequality and its criminalisation
blocks.rationale: Around 40 million people live in poverty; stakeholders report no measures on the structural drivers and expanding criminalisation of poverty.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 39 — Independent Expert on the enjoyment of human rights by persons with albinism: "income inequalities remained high in the United States, with some 40 million people reportedly living in poverty"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 39 — Special Rapporteur on racism: "referred to reports of the criminalization of poverty, which trapped people in the criminal justice system"

recommendations.text: Take holistic measures to eliminate rich-poor polarization and social inequality
End the criminalization of poverty, which disproportionately affects African-Americans
Introduce reforms to reverse the high rates of poverty and inequality and recognize economic, social and cultural rights internally

blocks.summary: Realise the right to housing and decriminalise homelessness
blocks.rationale: Governments at all levels are reported to have failed to meet the right to housing; laws banning sleeping in public spaces spread.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 42 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination; Human Rights Committee: "expressed concern about the high number of persons belonging to racial and ethnic minorities affected by homelessness and recommended abolishing laws and policies that criminalized homelessness"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 53 — Human Rights Watch: "governments at all levels had failed to meet the right to housing"

recommendations.text: Further enhance activities that will lead to reducing homelessness among vulnerable groups across the country

themes.theme: Right to an adequate standard of living

blocks.summary: Honour Indigenous treaties and guarantee free, prior and informed consent
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Executive Order 14112 on Tribal self-determination and funding was revoked in March 2025; FPIC is still not guaranteed in law or practice.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 58 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination; Human Rights Committee: "recommended that the United States honour the treaties entered into with Indigenous Peoples, guarantee, in law and in practice, the principle of free, prior and informed consent"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 83 — Several submissions (OHCHR summary): "Executive Order 14112, which had expanded access of Tribal Nations to federal funding and self-determination ... was revoked in March 2025"

recommendations.text: Develop strategies for addressing the housing and sanitary problems of marginalized communities such as indigenous and migrant communities

blocks.summary: Equitable, affordable access to health care
blocks.rationale: No move toward universal healthcare or nationwide Medicaid expansion; health inequities persist and 2025 brought cancellation of health grants.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 60 — Human Rights Watch: "systemic racism and the cost barriers of the predominantly for-profit health care system played a huge part in health inequities"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 59 — JS9; Human Rights Watch: "reported cancellation of grants for substance use and mental health programmes"

recommendations.text: Protect expanded and equitable access to health care
Take concrete steps to ensure the enjoyment of the human right to health by all its people without discrimination
Take further measures to make health-care services accessible to vulnerable people not supported by the current health system
Take measures for providing health-care services to all without prejudice to race, economic situation and citizenship status of persons under its jurisdiction
Step up its efforts, both at home and abroad, to improve the health, dignity and well-being of women, children and their families
Ensure access to health care, drugs and treatment to all segments of society

Continue its ongoing efforts to build a more inclusive society and reduce inequalities, including by updating its strategic plans to address the disproportionate impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on vulnerable populations
Ensure equal, full and rapid access for all segments of United States society to free health care in the face of the COVID-19 pandemic
Establish a public system that guarantees the right to health of its people, which has been decimated by the pandemic
Urge politicians to respect people ’ s right to life and right to health, and stop politicizing and stigmatizing the COVID-19 pandemic
Guarantee the right to health, even in the context of COVID-19
Make essential health services accessible to all women and girls, paying special attention to those who face multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination

blocks.summary: Access to abortion and maternal health care
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: The 2022 Dobbs decision removed the federal constitutional right to abortion; the Women's Health Protection Act did not pass and stakeholders report none of the supported SRHR recommendations were implemented.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 43 — Several special procedure mandate holders: "the United States Supreme Court decision to strike down Roe v. Wade represented a setback for the rule of law and for gender equality"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 57 — JS3: "none of the supported recommendations on sexual health and reproductive rights had been implemented"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 43 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended adopting the Women's Health Protection Act"

recommendations.text: Lift funding restrictions on United States foreign assistance to promote women ’ s full access to sexual and reproductive health and rights

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Clarify its approach to ensuring access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services

Ensure that laws permitting the refusal of care based on religious and moral beliefs do not restrict women ’ s sexual and reproductive health and rights and that measures are put in place to monitor and prevent violations of these rights

Reverse policies inhibiting comprehensive and universal access to voluntary sexual and reproductive health services, especially in emergency situations, and end related restrictions on foreign assistance

Take action to support equitable access to sexual and reproductive health and rights services, and review policies that effectively limit foreign assistance for sexual and reproductive health and rights services abroad
Rescind the Title X restrictions to ensure access to comprehensive family planning services for all
Ensure access by women and girls to sexual and reproductive rights and health
Protect the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women and girls by ensuring their access to sexual and reproductive health information, commodities and services
Guarantee essential health services for all, including sexual and reproductive health services
Ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health information, education and services for all
Ensure access by all women to sexual and reproductive health information and services

Repeal the Helms Amendment and the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance Policy and, in the interim, allow United States foreign assistance to be used, at a minimum, for safe abortion in cases of rape, incest and life endangerment
Ensure that its international aid allows access to sexual and reproductive health services

blocks.summary: Equitable, quality public education
blocks.rationale: Systemic funding inequities persist, book bans expanded, and the Department of Education is reported to be being dismantled.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 45 — Special Rapporteur on the right to education: "identified systemic inequalities in the education system, including inequitable funding, overreliance on standardized testing, discriminatory disciplinary practices and the diversion of public funds to private and charter schools"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 62 — JS6: "expressed concern at the dismantling of the Education Department"

recommendations.text: Take further robust and comprehensive measures to promote wider and equitable access to quality education at all levels

blocks.summary: Combat discrimination against women in work, pay and public life
blocks.rationale: Persistent discrimination in wages, employment and education is reported; no federal equal-pay legislation was enacted and DEI policies were revoked in 2025.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 75 — Elizka Relief Foundation: "persistent discrimination against women across various sectors such as wages, employment, and education"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 51 — Abshar; IESW: "recommended enacting federal legislation enforcing equal pay for equal work"

recommendations.text: Strengthen legislation in order to eliminate all forms of gender discrimination in employment
Explore the option of introducing a by-law on mandatory paid minimum maternity leave
Strengthen further equality in the workplace by moving towards universal paid maternity leave and advancing universal maternal health care
Continue reinforcing legislation to eliminate all forms of gender discrimination in employment and ensure equal pay for work of equal value in the workplace
Encourage further private employers to strengthen equality and to offer paid maternity leave

Implement fully the commitments in the women and peace and security agenda at the national and international levels, notably in the framework of its role as a member of the Security Council, and ensure – politically and financially – the participation of women in peace processes
Strengthen further the existing non-discriminatory, inclusive and integrated approach to work to ensure women ’ s equality and the promotion and protection of these rights

blocks.summary: Eliminate violence against women and girls
blocks.rationale: The Violence Against Women Act was reauthorised in 2022 with expanded tribal-jurisdiction provisions - a concrete step - but implementation gaps persist and 2025 brought funding cuts.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended intensifying efforts to prevent, combat and eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls, paying special attention to women from minority and marginalized groups"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 70 — GFG (Global Freedom Group): "reported funding cuts to the Violence Against Women Act and domestic violence programmes"

recommendations.text: Eliminate the wage gap and gender-based violence and guarantee access to justice and reparation for victims

blocks.summary: Women's participation in work and leadership
blocks.rationale: Persistent gender inequality in the workforce and leadership is reported, aggravated by the 2025 DEI revocation.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 76 — IPWR (Institute for Protection of Women's Rights): "the persistent gender inequality in the workforce ... Women, particularly women of colour, were significantly underrepresented in leadership roles and high-paying occupations"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts made and measures taken to ensure the protection of women ’ s and children ’ s rights

blocks.summary: Racial equity in child welfare and parental due process
blocks.rationale: Racial disparities in the child-welfare system persist; recommended due-process protections for parents were not adopted.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 54 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination: "expressed concern about the disproportionate number of children from racial and ethnic minorities removed from their families and placed in foster care"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 54 — Human Rights Committee: "recommended increasing due process protections for parents and reviewing the factors triggering child welfare interventions, in particular poverty and lack of financial resources"

recommendations.text: Create a federal mechanism to provide the necessary support to boys and young men in order to avoid any delay in their psychosocial development

blocks.summary: Honour Indigenous treaties and guarantee free, prior and informed consent
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Executive Order 14112 on Tribal self-determination and funding was revoked in March 2025; FPIC is still not guaranteed in law or practice.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 58 — Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination; Human Rights Committee: "recommended that the United States honour the treaties entered into with Indigenous Peoples, guarantee, in law and in practice, the principle of free, prior and informed consent"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 83 — Several submissions (OHCHR summary): "Executive Order 14112, which had expanded access of Tribal Nations to federal funding and self-determination ... was revoked in March 2025"

recommendations.text: Develop norms that ensure free, prior and informed consultations with indigenous communities in relation to projects with a potential impact on their territories and traditional ways of life, in accordance with Sustainable Development Goals 10 and 16

blocks.summary: Asylum access, immigration detention and deportations
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Measures run directly counter to these recommendations: asylum access was severely curtailed, detention without due process expanded and family separation resumed.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 69 — Human Rights Committee: "measures adopted to address migration challenges excessively restricted protection of the right to seek asylum and increased the risk of breaches of the principle of refoulement"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 64 — Several special procedure mandate holders: "the misuse of the Alien Enemies Act by the Government of the United States to deny due process and enable arbitrary deportations, involving enforced disappearances"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 90 — JS47: "at the US-Mexico border, asylum had been all but eliminated; migration enforcement escalated focusing on mass deportations"

recommendations.text: Step up measures to protect and ensure the rights of migrants
Strengthen the rights of migrant workers and their family members
Institute adequate mechanisms and means to deal with migratory flows in full respect with human dignity and international standards
End the zero-tolerance policy and protect the rights of migrants
Review administrative measures that criminally penalize migrants who enter the country without authorization
Ensure that detention conditions for immigrants, particularly for minors, comply with international human rights law
Increase its efforts to protect migrants, especially those in vulnerable groups, including by seeking alternatives to detention for migrant children and ensuring access to basic services

That the United States Department of Homeland Security and the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency should acknowledge the human right of families to remain united and/or be reunited
Stop incarcerating migrants, including migrant children, and guarantee the rights of migrants

Protect the rights of children who arrive in the United States and seek alternatives to the current detention system for migrant children, both unaccompanied and part of family groups, and allow them to remain under the protection of their parents
Fully guarantee the human rights and fundamental freedoms of migrant children and adolescents regardless of their immigration status
Ensure that detention centres for migrants and refugees and the treatment they receive meet the basic conditions called for under international human rights law and standards
Improve conditions of confinement pertaining to immigrants to meet human rights standards and international treaties
Stop separating young children from their migrant parents and putting them in cages
Include in legislation the ban on the separation of families in the context of migration

Guarantee respect for the life, dignity, security and human rights of migrants and refugees, ensure adequate conditions in detention centres, prioritize the family unit and safeguard the best interests of the child
Ensure the enjoyment of human rights by minorities and vulnerable groups in the country, especially those in detention centres for migrants along the southern border of the United States (Nicaragua).

blocks.summary: Protect access to asylum and non-refoulement; limit immigration detention
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Access to asylum was severely curtailed, detention without due process expanded and family separation resumed - directly contrary measures.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/2), para. 69 — Human Rights Committee: "measures adopted to address migration challenges excessively restricted protection of the right to seek asylum and increased the risk of breaches of the principle of refoulement"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/50/USA/3), para. 90 — JS47: "at the US-Mexico border, asylum had been all but eliminated"

recommendations.text: Make efforts in favour of the human rights of migrants, asylum seekers and refugees
Ensure that the detention and separation of migrant families and asylum seekers are not used as punitive measures to deter irregular entry into the country
Seek alternatives to the present immigration detention system and improve conditions of confinement to meet basic human rights standards
Stop the cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment of migrants and asylum seekers and the separation of hundreds of minors from their families

meta.round: First follow-up round. The Committee assessed the United States across further rounds (114th, 116th, 120th sessions); the grades below are the first-round evaluation.

paragraphs.title: Accountability for unlawful killing, torture and enforced disappearance
paragraphs.recommendation: Ensure that all cases of unlawful killing, torture or other ill-treatment, unlawful detention or enforced disappearance are effectively, independently and impartially investigated, perpetrators (including persons in positions of command) prosecuted and sanctioned, and victims provided with effective remedies; establish the responsibility of those who provided legal pretexts for manifestly illegal behaviour; incorporate the doctrine of “command responsibility”; and declassify and publish the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence report on the CIA secret detention programme.

limbs.eval: While noting, with appreciation, the recent prosecutions of law-enforcement officials and the conviction of four Blackwater USA contractors, the Committee requires information on investigations, prosecutions or convictions of Government personnel in positions of command.
The Committee requires information on measures taken to establish the responsibility of those who provided legal pretexts for manifestly illegal behaviour. It reiterates its recommendations.
The Committee regrets that no action has been taken to incorporate into its criminal law the doctrine of command responsibility for crimes under international law.

The Committee welcomes the declassification and release of over 500 pages of the report but is concerned that over 6,000 pages remain classified and that the Department of Justice does not plan to reopen investigations.

paragraphs.title: Right to life — gun violence and “Stand Your Ground” laws
paragraphs.recommendation: Effectively curb gun violence, including legislation requiring background checks for all private firearm transfers and strict enforcement of the Lautenberg Amendment; and review the Stand Your Ground laws to remove far-reaching immunity and ensure necessity and proportionality in the use of deadly force.

limbs.eval: While welcoming the Supreme Court decision upholding the federal domestic-violence firearms ban, the Committee requests information on new measures taken since the review and repeats its recommendations.
The Committee requests information on measures taken to implement the recommendation and is concerned that the immunity provided by stand-your-ground laws has, in some areas, expanded.

paragraphs.title: Guantánamo Bay — transfer, trial or release, and closure
paragraphs.recommendation: Expedite the transfer of detainees designated for transfer and the periodic-review process; ensure trial or immediate release and closure of the Guantánamo Bay facility; end administrative detention without charge or trial; and deal with criminal cases through the ordinary criminal justice system rather than military commissions.

limbs.eval: The Committee welcomes steps taken to expedite the review and transfer of detainees but is concerned that, at the current rate, review hearings would not be completed for all detainees until 2020. Updated statistical data is required.

limbs.limb: (b) end administrative detention; no military commissions
limbs.eval: The Committee regrets that persons continue to be held without charge or trial, in many cases for over a decade, and regrets the plans to continue prosecution by military commission, which is contrary to its recommendations.

paragraphs.title: Surveillance and the right to privacy (article 17)
paragraphs.recommendation: Bring surveillance activities within and outside the United States into conformity with article 17 (legality, proportionality, necessity, regardless of nationality or location); ensure interference is authorised by publicly accessible, precise law with effective safeguards; reform oversight to include judicial involvement; refrain from mandatory third-party data retention; and ensure effective remedies for abuse.

limbs.eval: While the Committee welcomes the administrative measures taken, it requires information on legislative measures to ensure the safeguards are provided for by law, and is concerned the administrative measures do not adequately protect article 17 rights.
No measures appear to have been taken since March 2014 to provide for judicial involvement in the authorization and monitoring of surveillance or to establish strong and independent oversight.
The Committee requires information on measures taken to stop the practice of mandatory retention of data by third parties.
No information was provided by the State party on access to remedies for persons affected in cases of abuse.
The Committee notes that the State party has not responded with regard to surveillance acts outside the United States and asks for more information.
